blocks.name: pc
blocks.description: Fetch-stage program counter. Holds the address of the instruction being fetched, always a multiple of two. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the held address becomes 80000000 hexadecimal, the first address of RAM; otherwise when trap_redirect is 1 it becomes trap_pc; otherwise when redirect is 1 it becomes redirect_pc; otherwise when stall is 1 it is left unchanged; otherwise it becomes the held address plus two when is16 is 1 and plus four when is16 is 0. trap_redirect comes from the write-back stage (an exception, an interrupt or mret) and so is older than redirect, which comes from the execute stage: when both are 1 the older one wins. is16 is 1 when the instruction being fetched is a 16-bit compressed instruction. pc is the held address. pc_plus4 is the address of the instruction after the one being fetched: the held address plus two when is16 is 1 and plus four when is16 is 0 (wrapping at 32 bits), available without waiting for a clock edge. trap_pc and redirect_pc are full 32-bit addresses and are loaded as they are, except that bit 0 of what is loaded is 0.

blocks.name: if_id
blocks.description: IF/ID pipeline register. Sits between the fetch stage and the decode stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: pc_out becomes 0; pc_plus4_out becomes 0; inst_out becomes 32'h00000013, the instruction addi x0, x0, 0, which changes nothing (a bubble). Otherwise, when stall is 1, every output keeps its value. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. A flush is how the instruction fetched on a wrong path is turned into a bubble. A further output, valid_out, is 0 after the register has been cleared (reset or flush) and becomes 1 at the first rising edge on which the register is loaded from its inputs (not cleared and not held); while stall holds the register, valid_out keeps its value. It tells the later stages that the instruction in this register is a real one and not a bubble.

blocks.name: ctrl_decode
blocks.description: Combinational instruction decoder. Reads the 32-bit instruction word and drives every control signal in the design, plus the three register selector fields. The register selectors are plain slices of the instruction: rs1 is bits 19:15, rs2 is bits 24:20 and rd is bits 11:7. Every control output's meaning is given by its own encoding table; decode the instruction's opcode field (bits 6:0), funct3 field (bits 14:12) and bit 30 and drive each control output to the code that matches. Most instruction words are not valid instructions, so the unrecognised case is not an edge case: an instruction the decoder does not recognise must drive regwrite to NO_WRITE, memwrite to NO_STORE, brsel to NO_BRANCH, pcsel to NEXT and memtype to NO_ACCESS, so that it changes no architectural state and touches no memory. For an unrecognised instruction immsel, memsrc, alusrc, arith and opsel are don't care: with nothing written and no jump taken, nothing reads them. An opcode alone does not make an instruction valid. For an opcode whose funct3 values are listed (branch, load, store, the two arithmetic opcodes, and the register jump, whose only listed value is 000), a funct3 value that is not listed for it (a store with a width code that is not byte, half or word, for example) makes the instruction unrecognised, and the unrecognised case above applies, not the values the opcode's class would give. For the upper-immediate loads and the direct jump, bits 14:12 are part of the immediate, not a function code: they never make the instruction unrecognised, and the outputs do not depend on them. Bit 30 of the instruction word is read only where the funct3 table says so (subtract, and arithmetic shift right); under any other funct3 it is ignored and never makes an instruction unrecognised. The arithmetic unit's result is consumed in only three places: written back when memsrc is FROM_ALU, used as a data memory address, and used as the jump target for JUMPREG. An instruction that uses none of the three (a conditional branch, which compares through the branch comparator, an upper-immediate load, and a direct jump) does not use the arithmetic unit, so for it alusrc, arith and opsel are don't care. The add-upper-immediate-to-pc instruction (opcode 0010111) is not an upper-immediate load: what it writes back is the address plus the immediate, computed by the arithmetic unit, so it does use the arithmetic unit, writes back FROM_ALU, and takes the immediate as its second operand. The register jump and link writes back the link address, the current address plus four, so it writes back FROM_PC; its jump target is the first register plus the immediate, computed by the arithmetic unit, so it also uses the arithmetic unit and takes the immediate as its second operand. The arithmetic unit's first operand is the register value for rs1, except for the add-upper-immediate-to-pc instruction, whose first operand is the address of the instruction itself: asel is USE_PC for that instruction and USE_REGISTER for every other instruction that uses the arithmetic unit; where the arithmetic unit is not used asel is don't care. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: hazard_unit
blocks.description: Combinational hazard unit. Decides when the front of the pipeline must wait and when its instructions must be thrown away. rs1_id and rs2_id are the source register numbers in the instruction in the decode stage. rd_ex, regwrite_ex and memsrc_ex are the destination register, the write enable and the write-back source of the instruction in the execute stage; is_csr_ex is 1 when that instruction is a CSR instruction, whose result is only available in the write-back stage. redirect is 1 when the execute stage has decided to take a branch or a jump. md_busy is 1 when the instruction in the execute stage is a multiply or divide whose result is not ready yet. wb_redirect is 1 when the write-back stage is taking an exception or mret. A load is an instruction whose memsrc is FROM_MEMORY. The load-use condition is 1 when the instruction in the execute stage writes a register (regwrite_ex is 1) and is a load (memsrc_ex is FROM_MEMORY) or a CSR instruction (is_csr_ex is 1), rd_ex is not zero, and rd_ex equals rs1_id or rs2_id: the value is not yet available to the instruction behind it, which must wait one cycle. The unit does not look at whether the instruction in the decode stage really reads rs1 or rs2, so it may stall once when it did not need to; it never fails to stall when it should. stall is 1 when the load-use condition is 1 or md_busy is 1: the program counter and the IF/ID register hold. md_stall equals md_busy: the ID/EX register holds. flush_if_id is 1 when redirect is 1 or wb_redirect is 1: the instruction fetched after the branch, or after the instruction that is trapping, is on the wrong path. flush_id_ex is 1 when redirect is 1, wb_redirect is 1 or the load-use condition is 1: after a redirect the instruction in the decode stage is on the wrong path, and for a load-use a bubble must go into the execute stage. flush_id_ex does not depend on md_busy, because while a multiply or divide waits the instruction in the execute stage must stay where it is. flush_ex_mem is 1 when md_busy is 1 or wb_redirect is 1: a bubble goes into the memory stage while a multiply or divide works and when an exception or mret is taken. flush_mem_wb equals wb_redirect: the instruction in the memory stage must not commit. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: id_ex
blocks.description: ID/EX pipeline register. Sits between the decode stage and the execute stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: is_amo_out becomes 0; amo_op_out becomes 0; irq_out becomes 0; pc_out becomes 0; pc_plus4_out becomes 0; rs1_data_out becomes 0; rs2_data_out becomes 0; imm_out becomes 0; rs1_out becomes 0; rs2_out becomes 0; rd_out becomes 0; regwrite_out becomes 0, NO_WRITE; alusrc_out becomes 0; arith_out becomes 0; opsel_out becomes 0; asel_out becomes 0; brsel_out becomes 7, NO_BRANCH; pcsel_out becomes 0, NEXT; memtype_out becomes 5, NO_ACCESS; memwrite_out becomes 0, NO_STORE; memsrc_out becomes 0; mdop_out becomes 0, MD_NONE; valid_out becomes 0, a bubble; inst_out becomes 0; xcpt_out becomes 0, no exception; cause_out becomes 0; csrop_out becomes 0, CSR_NONE; is_csr_out becomes 0; is_mret_out becomes 0; csr_imm_out becomes 0. Otherwise, when stall is 1, every output keeps its value. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. A cleared register holds a bubble: it writes no register, stores nothing, takes no branch, jumps nowhere, asks for no multiply or divide and raises no exception, whatever its other outputs read. A flush is used for the instruction behind a taken branch or jump, for the bubble after a load or CSR read that the next instruction needs, and when an exception or mret is taken. A stall holds the instruction in the execute stage while a multiply or divide is still working. valid is 1 for a real instruction and 0 for a bubble; xcpt is 1 when the instruction has raised an exception that will be taken when it reaches the write-back stage, with its cause in cause; csrop, csr_imm and is_csr say what a CSR instruction does; is_mret marks mret. A cleared register holds a bubble: valid, xcpt, csrop, is_csr and is_mret are 0. irq is 1 when the exception this instruction carries is really an interrupt that was attached to it in the decode stage (xcpt is then 1 too, and cause holds the interrupt's code); a cleared register holds irq 0. is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction and amo_op says which one (AMO_NONE for any other instruction); a cleared register holds is_amo 0 and amo_op 0.

blocks.name: forward_unit
blocks.description: Combinational forwarding unit. Decides, for each of the two operands of the instruction in the execute stage, whether to use the value read in the decode stage or a newer value that is still on its way to the register file. rs1 and rs2 are the source register numbers of the instruction in the execute stage. rd_mem and regwrite_mem are the destination register number and write enable of the instruction in the memory stage; rd_wb and regwrite_wb are those of the instruction in the write-back stage. fwd_a is for the first operand (rs1) and fwd_b for the second (rs2); the meaning of each code is given by its encoding table. For each operand: when regwrite_mem is 1, rd_mem is not zero and rd_mem equals the operand's register number, the code is FROM_EX_MEM; otherwise, when regwrite_wb is 1, rd_wb is not zero and rd_wb equals the operand's register number, the code is FROM_MEM_WB; otherwise the code is FROM_REGISTER. The memory stage wins over the write-back stage because it holds the newer instruction. Register zero is never forwarded, because it reads zero whatever is written to it. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: mem_wb
blocks.description: MEM/WB pipeline register. Sits between the memory stage and the write-back stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: irq_out becomes 0; result_out becomes 0; mem_rdata_out becomes 0; rd_out becomes 0; regwrite_out becomes 0, NO_WRITE; memsrc_out becomes 0; pc_out becomes 0; tval_out becomes 0; csr_wdata_out becomes 0; valid_out becomes 0, a bubble; inst_out becomes 0; xcpt_out becomes 0, no exception; cause_out becomes 0; csrop_out becomes 0, CSR_NONE; is_csr_out becomes 0; is_mret_out becomes 0. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. mem_rdata is the value the data memory read in the memory stage; result is the other write-back candidate. A flush puts a bubble into the write-back stage; it is used when an exception or mret is taken, so the instruction that was in the memory stage does not commit. pc is the instruction's own address, tval the trap value, csr_wdata the source value of a CSR instruction. valid is 1 for a real instruction and 0 for a bubble; xcpt is 1 when the instruction has raised an exception that will be taken when it reaches the write-back stage, with its cause in cause; csrop, csr_imm and is_csr say what a CSR instruction does; is_mret marks mret. A cleared register holds a bubble: valid, xcpt, csrop, is_csr and is_mret are 0. irq is 1 when the exception this instruction carries is really an interrupt that was attached to it in the decode stage (xcpt is then 1 too, and cause holds the interrupt's code); a cleared register holds irq 0.

blocks.name: md_decode
blocks.description: Combinational decoder for the multiply and divide instructions. inst is the 32-bit instruction word. mdop says whether it is one of the eight M-extension instructions and which one; the meaning of each code is given by its encoding table. An instruction is a multiply or divide only when bits 6:0 of inst are 0110011 and bits 31:25 are 0000001. For such an instruction the top bit of mdop is 1 and its low three bits are bits 14:12 of inst (the funct3 field), so funct3 000 is MUL, 001 is MULH, 010 is MULHSU, 011 is MULHU, 100 is DIV, 101 is DIVU, 110 is REM and 111 is REMU. For every other instruction word mdop is MD_NONE. The other reserved codes are never produced. No clock, no reset, no state.

encoding.1001: MULH: the high 32 bits of the product, both source registers read as signed
encoding.1010: MULHSU: the high 32 bits of the product, the first source register read as signed and the second as unsigned
encoding.1011: MULHU: the high 32 bits of the product, both source registers read as unsigned

blocks.name: booth_mul
blocks.description: Iterative multiplier using radix-4 Booth's algorithm: it forms the full 64-bit product of a and b, two multiplier bits per clock cycle. a_signed says whether a is read as a signed two's complement number (1) or as an unsigned number (0); b_signed says the same for b. Let A be the value of a read that way and B the value of b read that way. The product A times B, as a 64-bit two's complement number (its low 64 bits), is delivered as hi (bits 63:32) and lo (bits 31:0) while done is 1. The unit holds these values: a state that is IDLE, RUN or DONE; a 33-bit multiplicand M; a 34-bit multiplier register Q; a 36-bit accumulator ACC; one bit QM; a step counter. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the state becomes IDLE and M, Q, ACC, QM and the counter become zero. Otherwise, in IDLE: when start is 1 the unit copies its operands: M becomes the 33-bit value made of (a[31] and a_signed) followed by the 32 bits of a; Q becomes the 34-bit value made of two copies of (b[31] and b_signed) followed by the 32 bits of b; ACC becomes 0, QM becomes 0, the counter becomes 0 and the state becomes RUN; when start is 0 nothing changes. In RUN, one Booth step is made on every edge: look at the three bits Q[1], Q[0] and QM, in that order, read as a 3-bit number. T is a 36-bit value, wrapping, formed from ACC, MX (M sign-extended to 36 bits: its top bit M[32] copied into the three bits above it), and 2MX (MX shifted left one place, the top bit dropped, so a negative M gives a negative 2MX): for 000 and 111, T is ACC; for 001 and 010, T is ACC plus MX; for 011, T is ACC plus 2MX; for 100, T is ACC minus 2MX; for 101 and 110, T is ACC minus MX. Then ACC becomes T shifted right two places with its top bit kept (two copies of T[35] followed by T[35:2]), Q becomes T[1:0] followed by Q[33:2], QM becomes the old Q[1], and the counter goes up by one. When the counter was 16 before the step (this was the 17th step) the state becomes DONE. In DONE the state becomes IDLE on the next edge, whatever start is, and nothing else changes. Once a multiplication has begun it runs to the end whatever start does. done is 1 exactly when the state is DONE. While done is 1, ACC followed by Q read as one 70-bit number (ACC in the top 36 bits, Q in the low 34 bits) holds the product in its low 64 bits: lo is Q[31:0] and hi is ACC[29:0] followed by Q[33:32]. While done is 0, hi and lo are both 0. done, hi and lo depend only on the held state, not on the inputs.

blocks.name: iter_div
blocks.description: Iterative restoring divider: it divides a (the dividend) by b (the divisor) and delivers the quotient and remainder while done is 1, one quotient bit per clock cycle. is_signed says whether a and b are read as signed two's complement numbers (1) or as unsigned numbers (0). Results follow the RISC-V rules. For unsigned division the quotient is a divided by b rounded down and the remainder is a minus quotient times b. For signed division the quotient is rounded toward zero and the remainder has the sign of the dividend (or is zero). When b is 0 the quotient is all ones (FFFFFFFF) and the remainder is a, for signed and unsigned alike. When signed, a is the most negative number (80000000) and b is minus one (FFFFFFFF), the quotient is 80000000 and the remainder is 0. The unit holds: a state that is IDLE, RUN or DONE; a 33-bit remainder register R; a 32-bit quotient register Q; a 32-bit divisor register D; the original dividend A; flags neg_q, neg_r and by_zero; a step counter. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the state becomes IDLE and every held value becomes zero. Otherwise, in IDLE: when start is 1 the unit copies its operands: when is_signed is 1 and a[31] is 1, Q becomes the negation of a (32 bits, wrapping), else Q becomes a; when is_signed is 1 and b[31] is 1, D becomes the negation of b, else D becomes b; R becomes 0; A becomes a; neg_q becomes 1 when is_signed is 1 and a[31] differs from b[31], else 0; neg_r becomes 1 when is_signed is 1 and a[31] is 1, else 0; by_zero becomes 1 when b is 0, else 0; the counter becomes 0; the state becomes RUN. When start is 0 nothing changes. In RUN, one step is made on every edge: S is the 33-bit value R[31:0] followed by Q[31]. When S is at least D (D taken as an unsigned number, zero-extended to 33 bits), R becomes S minus D and the new Q bit is 1; otherwise R becomes S and the new Q bit is 0. Q becomes Q[30:0] followed by the new bit, and the counter goes up by one. When the counter was 31 before the step (this was the 32nd step) the state becomes DONE. In DONE the state becomes IDLE on the next edge, whatever start is, and nothing else changes. Once a division has begun it runs to the end whatever start does. done is 1 exactly when the state is DONE. While done is 1: when by_zero is 1 the quotient is FFFFFFFF and the remainder is A; otherwise the quotient is Q, negated (32 bits, wrapping) when neg_q is 1, and the remainder is R[31:0], negated when neg_r is 1. While done is 0, quotient and remainder are both 0. done, quotient and remainder depend only on the held state, not on the inputs.

blocks.name: md_ctrl
blocks.description: Combinational control for the multiply and divide units, in the execute stage. mdop is the instruction's multiply or divide code, whose meaning is given by its encoding table. is_md is 1 when mdop is any of the eight operations (its top bit is 1). start_mul is 1 when is_md is 1 and the operation is a multiply (MUL, MULH, MULHSU or MULHU, bit 2 of mdop is 0); start_div is 1 when is_md is 1 and the operation is a divide or remainder (DIV, DIVU, REM or REMU, bit 2 of mdop is 1). For the multiplier, mul_a_signed is 1 for MUL, MULH and MULHSU and 0 for every other mdop value (including all four divides and every value that is not a multiply or divide); mul_b_signed is 1 for MUL and MULH and 0 for every other mdop value; div_signed is 1 for DIV and REM and 0 for every other mdop value. done is mul_done when start_mul is 1, div_done when start_div is 1, and 0 otherwise. busy is 1 when is_md is 1 and done is 0: the instruction is waiting for its result. md_result is the instruction's result: for MUL it is mul_lo; for MULH, MULHSU and MULHU it is mul_hi; for DIV and DIVU it is quotient; for REM and REMU it is remainder; for every other mdop it is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: regwrite_merge
blocks.description: Combinational. regwrite is the logical OR of the three inputs ctrl_regwrite, is_csr and is_amo: it is 1 when at least one of them is 1, and 0 only when all three are 0. blocks.name: md_reset
blocks.description: Combinational. unit_reset is 1 when sys_reset is 1 or kill is 1, and 0 otherwise: a multiply or divide that is in progress when an exception or mret is taken is abandoned in the way a reset abandons it. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: kill_gate
blocks.description: Combinational. Two kill inputs. kill_wb is 1 when a trap or mret is taken: it cancels the register write of the instruction in write-back (regwrite_out is regwrite when kill_wb is 0 and 0 when kill_wb is 1). kill_mem is 1 for any redirect, including a CSR refetch: it cancels the memory write of the instruction in the memory stage (memwrite_out is memwrite when kill_mem is 0 and 0 when kill_mem is 1). blocks.name: wb_csr_mux

blocks.name: csr_inflight
blocks.description: Combinational. busy is 1 when any of the six inputs is 1, and 0 otherwise. The inputs say whether the instruction in the execute stage, the memory stage and the write-back stage is a CSR instruction or an mret: instructions that can change the interrupt enables. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: irq_gate
blocks.description: Combinational, in the decode stage. valid is 1 when the instruction in decode is a real one and not a bubble. dec_xcpt and dec_cause are the exception, if any, that the instruction's own decode found. pending and irq_cause say whether an interrupt is pending and enabled and which (irq_cause is a cause code). busy is 1 when an older instruction that can change the interrupt enables is still in flight. take is 1 when valid is 1, pending is 1 and busy is 0: the interrupt is attached to this instruction. xcpt is 1 when take is 1 or dec_xcpt is 1. cause is irq_cause when take is 1 and dec_cause otherwise. irq equals take. blocks.name: fetch_next_word
blocks.description: Combinational. pc is the address being fetched (a multiple of two). hi_addr is pc plus four (wrapping at 32 bits): the address at which the second copy of the instruction memory is read, so that it answers with the word after the one that holds pc. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fetch_align
blocks.description: Combinational. pc is the address being fetched (a multiple of two). word_lo is the 32-bit word of the instruction memory that holds the address pc (the word at pc with bits 1:0 cleared) and word_hi is the word after it. inst is the 32 bits of instruction text that start at pc: when bit 1 of pc is 0 it is word_lo, and when bit 1 of pc is 1 it is word_hi bits 15:0 as the upper half and word_lo bits 31:16 as the lower half, that is {word_hi[15:0], word_lo[31:16]}. is16 is 1 when bits 1:0 of inst are not 11, which is how a 16-bit compressed instruction is told from a 32-bit one. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_q0
blocks.description: Combinational expander for the compressed instructions of one quadrant. inst is a 32-bit value of which only bits 15:2 are read: bits 1:0 are not looked at, and this block always acts as the decoder for the instructions whose bits 1:0 are 00. Write h for the 16-bit compressed instruction {inst[15:2], 2'b00}, so h[1:0] is 00 and h[k] is inst[k] for k from 2 to 15. word is the 32-bit RISC-V instruction h stands for, or, when h is reserved or not available on this core, the 16-bit value h zero-extended to 32 bits (word is then {16'b0, h}). Let f3 be h[15:13], rdp be h[4:2] + 8, rs1p be h[9:7] + 8 and rs2p be h[4:2] + 8. f3 = 000 is C.ADDI4SPN: let imm10 be the 10-bit value {h[10:7], h[12:11], h[5], h[6], 2'b00}; when imm10 is 0 the instruction is reserved, otherwise word is the I-type instruction addi rdp, x2, imm10 (the 12-bit immediate is imm10 zero-extended, opcode 0010011, funct3 000, rs1 is x2). f3 = 010 is C.LW: let imm7 be the 7-bit value {h[5], h[12:10], h[6], 2'b00}; word is the I-type lw rdp, imm7(rs1p) (immediate imm7 zero-extended to 12 bits, opcode 0000011, funct3 010). f3 = 110 is C.SW: with the same imm7, word is the S-type sw rs2p, imm7(rs1p) (immediate imm7 zero-extended to 12 bits, opcode 0100011, funct3 010). Every other value of f3 (001, 011, 100, 101, 111) is reserved or needs a floating-point extension this core does not have. Registers written x0 to x31 are 5-bit numbers; a compact register number from a 3-bit field c is c + 8. Instruction layouts: I-type is {imm[11:0], rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}; S-type is {imm[11:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:0], opcode}; B-type is {imm[12], imm[10:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:1], imm[11], opcode}; U-type is {imm[31:12], rd, opcode}; J-type is {imm[20], imm[10:1], imm[11], imm[19:12], rd, opcode}; R-type is {funct7, rs2, rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_q1
blocks.description: Combinational expander for the compressed instructions of one quadrant. inst is a 32-bit value of which only bits 15:2 are read: bits 1:0 are not looked at, and this block always acts as the decoder for the instructions whose bits 1:0 are 01. Write h for the 16-bit compressed instruction {inst[15:2], 2'b01}, so h[1:0] is 01 and h[k] is inst[k] for k from 2 to 15. word is the 32-bit RISC-V instruction h stands for, or, when h is reserved or not available on this core, the 16-bit value h zero-extended to 32 bits (word is then {16'b0, h}). Let f3 be h[15:13] and rd be h[11:7]. Let imm6 be the 6-bit value {h[12], h[6:2]} and simm be imm6 sign-extended to 12 bits. f3 = 000 is C.ADDI (and C.NOP): word is the I-type addi rd, rd, simm (opcode 0010011, funct3 000). f3 = 010 is C.LI: word is the I-type addi rd, x0, simm. f3 = 001 is C.JAL and f3 = 101 is C.J: let off12 be the 12-bit value {h[12], h[8], h[10:9], h[6], h[7], h[2], h[11], h[5:3], 1'b0} and joff be off12 sign-extended to 21 bits; word is the J-type jal with immediate joff (opcode 1101111) and rd x1 for C.JAL, x0 for C.J. f3 = 011: when rd is 2 this is C.ADDI16SP: let imm10 be the 10-bit value {h[12], h[4:3], h[5], h[2], h[6], 4'b0000}; when imm10 is 0 the instruction is reserved, otherwise word is the I-type addi x2, x2, imm10 sign-extended to 12 bits; when rd is not 2 this is C.LUI: when imm6 is 0 the instruction is reserved, otherwise word is the U-type lui rd with the 20-bit immediate imm6 sign-extended to 20 bits (opcode 0110111). f3 = 100 is the group of arithmetic instructions on compact registers: let rdq be h[9:7] + 8, rs2q be h[4:2] + 8 and shamt be h[6:2]. When h[11:10] is 00 (C.SRLI): reserved if h[12] is 1, otherwise word is the I-type srli rdq, rdq, shamt, whose immediate field is {7'b0000000, shamt} (opcode 0010011, funct3 101). When h[11:10] is 01 (C.SRAI): reserved if h[12] is 1, otherwise the I-type srai rdq, rdq, shamt whose immediate field is {7'b0100000, shamt} (opcode 0010011, funct3 101). When h[11:10] is 10 (C.ANDI): word is the I-type andi rdq, rdq, simm (opcode 0010011, funct3 111). When h[11:10] is 11: reserved if h[12] is 1; otherwise the R-type instruction (opcode 0110011, rs1 and rd both rdq, rs2 rs2q) chosen by h[6:5]: 00 sub (funct7 0100000, funct3 000), 01 xor (funct7 0000000, funct3 100), 10 or (funct7 0000000, funct3 110), 11 and (funct7 0000000, funct3 111). f3 = 110 is C.BEQZ and f3 = 111 is C.BNEZ: let off9 be the 9-bit value {h[12], h[6:5], h[2], h[11:10], h[4:3], 1'b0} and boff be off9 sign-extended to 13 bits; let rs1q be h[9:7] + 8; word is the B-type branch with immediate boff, rs1 rs1q, rs2 x0 and opcode 1100011, with funct3 000 (beq) for C.BEQZ and 001 (bne) for C.BNEZ. Registers written x0 to x31 are 5-bit numbers; a compact register number from a 3-bit field c is c + 8. Instruction layouts: I-type is {imm[11:0], rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}; S-type is {imm[11:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:0], opcode}; B-type is {imm[12], imm[10:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:1], imm[11], opcode}; U-type is {imm[31:12], rd, opcode}; J-type is {imm[20], imm[10:1], imm[11], imm[19:12], rd, opcode}; R-type is {funct7, rs2, rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_q2
blocks.description: Combinational expander for the compressed instructions of one quadrant. inst is a 32-bit value of which only bits 15:2 are read: bits 1:0 are not looked at, and this block always acts as the decoder for the instructions whose bits 1:0 are 10. Write h for the 16-bit compressed instruction {inst[15:2], 2'b10}, so h[1:0] is 10 and h[k] is inst[k] for k from 2 to 15. word is the 32-bit RISC-V instruction h stands for, or, when h is reserved or not available on this core, the 16-bit value h zero-extended to 32 bits (word is then {16'b0, h}). Let f3 be h[15:13], rd be h[11:7] and rs2 be h[6:2]. f3 = 000 is C.SLLI: reserved if h[12] is 1, otherwise word is the I-type slli rd, rd, shamt with shamt h[6:2], whose immediate field is {7'b0000000, h[6:2]} (opcode 0010011, funct3 001). f3 = 010 is C.LWSP: reserved when rd is 0; otherwise let off8 be the 8-bit value {h[3:2], h[12], h[6:4], 2'b00} and word be the I-type lw rd, off8(x2) (immediate off8 zero-extended to 12 bits, rs1 x2, opcode 0000011, funct3 010). f3 = 100: when h[12] is 0 and rs2 is 0 this is C.JR: reserved when rd is 0, otherwise word is the I-type jalr x0, 0(rd) (opcode 1100111, funct3 000, immediate 0, rd field x0, rs1 rd); when h[12] is 0 and rs2 is not 0 this is C.MV: word is the R-type add rd, x0, rs2 (funct7 0000000, funct3 000, opcode 0110011); when h[12] is 1 and rs2 is 0 and rd is 0 this is C.EBREAK: word is 32'h00100073; when h[12] is 1 and rs2 is 0 and rd is not 0 this is C.JALR: word is the I-type jalr x1, 0(rd) (opcode 1100111, funct3 000, immediate 0, rd field x1, rs1 rd); when h[12] is 1 and rs2 is not 0 this is C.ADD: word is the R-type add rd, rd, rs2 (funct7 0000000, funct3 000, opcode 0110011). f3 = 110 is C.SWSP: let off8 be the 8-bit value {h[8:7], h[12:9], 2'b00}; word is the S-type sw rs2, off8(x2) (immediate off8 zero-extended to 12 bits, rs1 x2, funct3 010, opcode 0100011). Every other value of f3 (001, 011, 101, 111) is reserved or needs a floating-point extension this core does not have. Registers written x0 to x31 are 5-bit numbers; a compact register number from a 3-bit field c is c + 8. Instruction layouts: I-type is {imm[11:0], rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}; S-type is {imm[11:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:0], opcode}; B-type is {imm[12], imm[10:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:1], imm[11], opcode}; U-type is {imm[31:12], rd, opcode}; J-type is {imm[20], imm[10:1], imm[11], imm[19:12], rd, opcode}; R-type is {funct7, rs2, rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_select
blocks.description: Combinational. inst is the 32 bits of instruction text from the fetch aligner, and q0, q1 and q2 are the expanded forms of its low half in each compressed quadrant. inst_out is inst when bits 1:0 of inst are 11 (a 32-bit instruction), q0 when they are 00, q1 when they are 01 and q2 when they are 10. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: io_load
blocks.description: Combinational. raw is what a device register returned, already in its low bits. memtype is the access type of the load, with the meaning its encoding table gives. rdata is: for MEM_BYTE, raw bits 7:0 sign-extended to 32 bits; for MEM_BYTE_U, raw bits 7:0 zero-extended; for MEM_HALF, raw bits 15:0 sign-extended; for MEM_HALF_U, raw bits 15:0 zero-extended; for every other code (MEM_WORD, NO_ACCESS and the reserved codes) raw unchanged. The low address bits are not used: a device returns the register's value in the low bits whichever byte of the word was addressed. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: load_sel
blocks.description: Load value selector: the data memory's value, or a device's.

blocks.name: amo_ctl
blocks.description: Combinational. is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction. The other inputs are what the ordinary decoder drives; each output is that input, except that when is_amo is 1 the outputs are: immsel_out NO_IMMEDIATE (101), alusrc_out USE_IMMEDIATE (1), arith_out LOGICAL (0), opsel_out ADD_SUB (000), asel_out USE_REGISTER (0), memtype_out MEM_WORD (010), memsrc_out FROM_MEMORY (01) and memwrite_out NO_STORE (0). That makes the arithmetic unit compute rs1 plus zero, the address of the atomic access. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: amo_active
blocks.description: Combinational. active is 1 when the instruction in the memory stage performs its atomic access: valid is 1 and is_amo is 1 and sel_ram is 1 and xcpt is 0 and kill is 0, and 0 otherwise. valid is 1 when the instruction is a real one, is_amo is 1 when it is an atomic instruction, sel_ram is 1 when its address is in RAM, xcpt is 1 when it has raised an exception and kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: amo_core
blocks.description: Combinational. Atomic memory operations in the memory stage. active is 1 when the instruction performs its atomic access, is_amo is 1 when it is an atomic instruction and amo_op says which (the meaning is given by its encoding table). rs2 is the value of the instruction's second register. old is the 32-bit word the data memory reads at the address of the access. kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back. match is 1 when the reservation held for the address of this access matches it. Outputs: use_sc is 1 when is_amo is 1 and amo_op is AMO_SC, and 0 otherwise; sc_result is 0 when match is 1 and 1 otherwise (as a 32-bit value); we is 1 when active is 1 and either amo_op is one of AMO_SWAP, AMO_ADD, AMO_XOR, AMO_AND, AMO_OR, AMO_MIN, AMO_MAX, AMO_MINU, AMO_MAXU, or amo_op is AMO_SC and match is 1, and 0 otherwise; wdata is the new word: for AMO_SWAP rs2, AMO_ADD old plus rs2 (wrapping at 32 bits), AMO_XOR old xor rs2, AMO_AND old and rs2, AMO_OR old or rs2, AMO_MIN the smaller of old and rs2 read as signed 32-bit values, AMO_MAX the larger, AMO_MINU the smaller read as unsigned, AMO_MAXU the larger read as unsigned, and for every other amo_op (AMO_SC, AMO_LR, AMO_NONE, the reserved codes) rs2; set_rsv is 1 when active is 1 and amo_op is AMO_LR, and 0 otherwise; clr_rsv is 1 when kill is 1, or when active is 1 and amo_op is AMO_SC, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

semantics.description: Which atomic memory operation an instruction is, or that it is not an atomic instruction.

encoding.0001: AMO_LR: load-reserved: load the word and record a reservation on its address
encoding.0010: AMO_SC: store-conditional: store only if the reservation holds, and write back 0 for success or 1 for failure
encoding.0011: AMO_SWAP: write the second register's value, write back the old value
encoding.0100: AMO_ADD: write old plus the second register, write back the old value
encoding.0101: AMO_XOR: write old exclusive-or the second register, write back the old value
encoding.0110: AMO_AND: write old and the second register, write back the old value
encoding.0111: AMO_OR: write old or the second register, write back the old value
encoding.1000: AMO_MIN: write the smaller of old and the second register, both signed, write back the old value
encoding.1001: AMO_MAX: write the larger of old and the second register, both signed, write back the old value
encoding.1010: AMO_MINU: write the smaller of old and the second register, both unsigned, write back the old value
encoding.1011: AMO_MAXU: write the larger of old and the second register, both unsigned, write back the old value

blocks.name: amo_match
blocks.description: Combinational. match is 1 when rsv_valid is 1 and bits 31:2 of addr equal bits 31:2 of rsv_addr, and 0 otherwise (bits 1:0 of both are not looked at). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: wdata_sel
blocks.description: Data memory write value: the store data, or the new word of an atomic operation.

blocks.name: sc_sel
blocks.description: Write-back value of the memory stage: the loaded value, or the result of a store-conditional.

blocks.name: ram_we_merge
blocks.description: Combinational. we is 1 when store_we is 1 or amo_we is 1, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: mem_req
blocks.description: Combinational. Says whether the instruction in the memory stage asks for the shared bus. valid is 1 when the instruction is a real one, xcpt is 1 when it has raised an exception, kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back, memsrc is the write-back source of the instruction (a load is 01), memwrite is 1 for a store that is really going to happen, is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction. req is 1 when valid is 1, xcpt is 0, kill is 0 and (memsrc is 01 or memwrite is 1 or is_amo is 1), and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: pmp_regs
blocks.description: The physical memory protection registers that exist so far: pmpcfg0 (32 bits, four entry configurations) and pmpaddr0 (32 bits). Both are held state, 0 at reset. On each rising clock edge: rst is 1: both become 0. Otherwise, when we is 1 and sel (6 bits) is 42, pmpcfg0 takes nval (32 bits); when we is 1 and sel is 43, pmpaddr0 takes nval; any other case keeps its value. The outputs show the held values. Access checks are not part of this block.

blocks.name: sys_decode
blocks.description: Combinational decoder for the instructions that are illegal, trap or touch the control and status registers, for a core with user, supervisor and machine modes. inst is the 32-bit instruction word; priv (2 bits) is the privilege level (0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine; 2 is treated as 3). The word is LEGAL when bits 1:0 are 11 and it matches one of these (opcode is bits 6:0, funct3 bits 14:12, funct7 bits 31:25): LUI (opcode 0110111), AUIPC (0010111) and JAL (1101111) with any other bits; JALR (1100111) with funct3 000; a branch (1100011) with funct3 000, 001, 100, 101, 110 or 111; a load (0000011) with funct3 000, 001, 010, 100 or 101; a store (0100011) with funct3 000, 001 or 010; an immediate arithmetic instruction (0010011) with funct3 000, 010, 011, 100, 110 or 111 and any upper bits, with funct3 001 and funct7 0000000, or with funct3 101 and funct7 0000000 or 0100000; a register arithmetic instruction (0110011) with funct7 0000000 and any funct3, with funct7 0100000 and funct3 000 or 101, or with funct7 0000001 and any funct3; a fence (opcode 0001111, funct3 000) or fence.i (opcode 0001111, funct3 001); an atomic instruction (opcode 0101111) with funct3 010 and bits 31:27 equal to 00000, 00001, 00011, 00100, 01000, 01100, 10000, 10100, 11000 or 11100 (bits 26:25 may be anything), or with bits 31:27 equal to 00010 and bits 24:20 equal to 00000; a system instruction (1110011) with funct3 000 that is exactly one of five words: 00000073 hexadecimal (ecall), 00100073 (ebreak), 30200073 (mret), 10200073 (sret), 10500073 (wfi), or that is sfence.vma: funct7 0001001, bits 11:7 00000 and funct3 000 (bits 24:15 may be anything); a system instruction with funct3 001, 010, 011, 101, 110 or 111 (the six CSR instructions, bits 31:20 are the CSR address and bits 19:15 the source register or immediate); or a fetch-fault word: opcode 0001011 with funct3 001 or 010 (every other bit may be anything). Every other word is illegal. Outputs, the first case that applies: an illegal word: xcpt 1, cause 2 (ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION). A fetch-fault word: xcpt 1, cause 12 (1100) when funct3 is 001 and cause 1 when funct3 is 010. ebreak: xcpt 1, cause 3. ecall: xcpt 1, cause 8 when priv is 0, 9 when priv is 1, 11 when priv is 2 or 3. sret: csrop 101. sfence.vma: csrop 110. fence.i: csrop 111. A CSR instruction: is_csr 1; csr_imm is funct3 bit 2; csrop is 010 (CSR_WRITE) when funct3 bits 1:0 are 01, 011 (CSR_SET) when they are 10 and bits 19:15 are not zero, 100 (CSR_CLEAR) when they are 11 and bits 19:15 are not zero, and 001 (CSR_READ) when they are 10 or 11 and bits 19:15 are zero. Every output a case does not name is 0 (xcpt, cause, csrop, csr_imm, is_csr); fence, wfi, mret and the atomics have them all 0. Independently of those cases: is_mret is 1 only for the word 30200073. is_amo is 1 for a legal atomic instruction, and amo_op is then, by bits 31:27: 00010 AMO_LR (0001), 00011 AMO_SC (0010), 00001 AMO_SWAP (0011), 00000 AMO_ADD (0100), 00100 AMO_XOR (0101), 01100 AMO_AND (0110), 01000 AMO_OR (0111), 10000 AMO_MIN (1000), 10100 AMO_MAX (1001), 11000 AMO_MINU (1010), 11100 AMO_MAXU (1011); for every other word is_amo and amo_op are 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ex_xcpt
blocks.description: Combinational exception unit for the execute stage of a core with an MMU. It adds the exceptions the execute stage finds to the one decode may already have raised, and decides the trap value. id_xcpt and id_cause (4 bits) are decode's exception; id_irq is 1 when that is really an interrupt. inst and pc are the instruction and its address. memtype (3 bits) is the access type (101 when the instruction is not a load or store), memwrite is 1 for a store, alu_y is the (virtual) address of the access. d_pf and d_af say the access gave a page fault or an access fault in translation, and d_store says it counts as a store. A memory access is misaligned when memtype is 010, 110 or 111 and bits 1:0 of alu_y are not 00, or memtype is 001 or 100 and bit 0 of alu_y is 1; memtype 000, 011 and 101 are never misaligned. The first that applies: (1) id_xcpt is 1: xcpt 1, cause id_cause; tval is 0 when id_irq is 1; otherwise inst when id_cause is 2, pc when it is 3, pc plus 2 (32 bits, wrapping) when id_cause is 12 or 1 and bit 20 of inst is 1, pc when id_cause is 12 or 1 and bit 20 of inst is 0, and 0 for any other cause. (2) misaligned: xcpt 1, cause 6 when memwrite is 1 and 4 otherwise, tval alu_y. (3) d_pf is 1: xcpt 1, cause 15 when d_store is 1 and 13 otherwise, tval alu_y. (4) d_af is 1: xcpt 1, cause 7 when d_store is 1 and 5 otherwise, tval alu_y. (5) otherwise xcpt, cause and tval are 0. memwrite_out is 0 when xcpt is 1 and memwrite otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: csr_sel2
blocks.description: Combinational. The CSR a CSR instruction names, and whether the access is illegal. a is bits 31:20 of inst (the CSR address). The CSR numbers (sel): 300 hexadecimal mstatus 1, 301 misa 2, 302 medeleg 3, 303 mideleg 4, 304 mie 5, 305 mtvec 6, 306 mcounteren 7, 340 mscratch 8, 341 mepc 9, 342 mcause 10, 343 mtval 11, 344 mip 12, B00 mcycle 13, B02 minstret 14, B80 mcycleh 15, B82 minstreth 16, C00 cycle 17, C01 time 18, C02 instret 19, C80 cycleh 20, C81 timeh 21, C82 instreth 22, F11 mvendorid 23, F12 marchid 24, F13 mimpid 25, F14 mhartid 26, 100 sstatus 27, 104 sie 28, 105 stvec 29, 106 scounteren 30, 140 sscratch 31, 141 sepc 32, 142 scause 33, 143 stval 34, 144 sip 35, 180 satp 36, 7A0 tselect 37, 7A1 tdata1 38, 7A2 tdata2 39, 7A3 tdata3 40, 320 mcountinhibit 41 (these five are hard-wired: they read 0 and ignore writes), 3A0 pmpcfg0 42, 3B0 pmpaddr0 43; every other address is 0 (no register). sel (6 bits) is the number for a. csrop (3 bits) is the instruction's CSR operation: 000 none, 001 CSR read only, 010 CSR write, 011 CSR set bits, 100 CSR clear bits, 101 sret, 110 sfence.vma, 111 fence.i. priv (2 bits) is the privilege level (0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine). An access is a csrop of 001, 010, 011 or 100; a write is a csrop of 010, 011 or 100. The access is bad when any of these holds: sel is 0; priv is less than bits 9:8 of a; it is a write and bits 11:10 of a are 11; sel is 36 (satp) and priv is 1 and tvm is 1; sel is a counter (17 to 22) and priv is not 3 and either bit b of mcounteren is 0, or priv is 0 and bit b of scounteren is 0, where b is 0 for cycle and cycleh (17, 20), 1 for time and timeh (18, 21) and 2 for instret and instreth (19, 22). illegal is 1 when the instruction is an access and the access is bad, and 0 otherwise (in particular 0 for every csrop that is not an access). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: csr_hw
blocks.description: Combinational. Maps the CSR addresses of the hard-wired performance, endianness and environment-configuration registers (they read 0 and ignore writes) onto number 44, after the CSR decoder. inst (32 bits) is an instruction; a is its bits 31:20 (the CSR address). sel_in (6 bits) and ill_in (1 bit) are the decoder's number and illegal flag. csrop (3 bits) is 000 none, 001 CSR read only, 010 CSR write, 011 CSR set bits, 100 CSR clear bits, other values not a CSR access; priv (2 bits) is the privilege level (3 machine). hw is 1 when a is 310, 30A, 31A or 10A hexadecimal, or from 323 to 33F, or from B03 to B1F, or from B83 to B9F, or from C03 to C1F, or from C83 to C9F (all hexadecimal, bounds included). When sel_in is 0 and hw is 1: sel_out is 44 and ill_out is 1 when csrop is 001, 010, 011 or 100 and priv is not 3, or when csrop is 010, 011 or 100 and bits 11:10 of a are 11 (a read-only address written), else 0. In every other case sel_out is sel_in and ill_out is ill_in. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: csr_alu
blocks.description: Combinational. The value a CSR instruction writes. old is the register's value before the instruction, src the instruction's source value (32 bits each). csrop (3 bits) is the instruction's CSR operation: 000 none, 001 CSR read only, 010 CSR write, 011 CSR set bits, 100 CSR clear bits, 101 sret, 110 sfence.vma, 111 fence.i. nval is src when csrop is 010, old OR src when csrop is 011, old AND NOT src when csrop is 100, and old for every other csrop. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: irq_select
blocks.description: Combinational. Which interrupt is taken, with delegation to supervisor mode. mip, mie and mideleg are 12 bits each, with an interrupt per odd bit: bit 1 supervisor software (SSI), bit 3 machine software (MSI), bit 5 supervisor timer (STI), bit 7 machine timer (MTI), bit 9 supervisor external (SEI), bit 11 machine external (MEI); the even bits do not matter. priv is the privilege level (2 bits: 0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine). An interrupt c is pending when bit c of mip and bit c of mie are both 1. A pending interrupt c is enabled when: if bit c of mideleg is 1, priv is 0, or priv is 1 and mstatus_sie is 1; if bit c of mideleg is 0, priv is not 3, or mstatus_mie is 1. The interrupts are looked at in the order 11, 3, 7, 9, 1, 5, and the first that is pending and enabled is taken: pending is 1 and cause (4 bits) is its number c. When none is, pending is 0 and cause is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: mstatus_reg
blocks.description: The privilege level and the mstatus register. Held state: priv (2 bits) and mstatus (32 bits, of which only these bits are held, every other bit is always 0: SIE bit 1, MIE bit 3, SPIE bit 5, MPIE bit 7, SPP bit 8, MPP bits 12:11, MPRV bit 17, SUM bit 18, MXR bit 19, TVM bit 20, TW bit 21, TSR bit 22). Outputs show the held state: priv, mstatus, and its fields mie (bit 3), sie (bit 1), mprv (bit 17), mpp (bits 12:11, 2 bits), sum (bit 18), mxr (bit 19), tvm (bit 20), tw (bit 21), tsr (bit 22). On each rising clock edge, the first that applies: rst is 1: priv becomes 3 and mstatus 0. trap_m is 1: MPIE takes the old MIE, MIE becomes 0, MPP takes the old priv, priv becomes 3. trap_s is 1: SPIE takes the old SIE, SIE becomes 0, SPP takes bit 0 of the old priv, priv becomes 1. mret is 1: priv takes the old MPP, MIE takes the old MPIE, MPIE becomes 1, MPP becomes 0, and when the old MPP is not 3, MPRV becomes 0. sret is 1: priv takes the old SPP (0 or 1), SIE takes the old SPIE, SPIE becomes 1, SPP becomes 0, MPRV becomes 0. we_m is 1 (a write to mstatus): every held bit takes the same bit of wdata, except that when bits 12:11 of wdata are 10 MPP keeps its old value. we_s is 1 (a write to sstatus): SIE, SPIE, SPP, SUM and MXR take the same bits of wdata and every other held bit keeps its value. Otherwise nothing changes. Fields not named in a case keep their values.

blocks.name: trap_unit
blocks.description: Combinational. What the write-back stage does with its instruction. valid is 1 for a real instruction. xcpt is 1 when it carries an exception or an interrupt, with irq 1 for an interrupt, cause (4 bits) its code, tval (32 bits) its trap value. irq is 1 only together with xcpt, and then cause is one of the interrupt codes 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 or 11 (0001, 0011, 0101, 0111, 1001, 1011). pc and inst are the instruction's address and word. csrop (3 bits) is the instruction's CSR operation: 000 none, 001 CSR read only, 010 CSR write, 011 CSR set bits, 100 CSR clear bits, 101 sret, 110 sfence.vma, 111 fence.i. is_mret is 1 for mret. illegal_csr is 1 when its CSR access is illegal. priv (2 bits: 0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine), tsr and tvm are from mstatus; medeleg (16 bits) and mideleg (12 bits) the delegation registers; mtvec, stvec, mepc and sepc (32 bits each) the trap vectors and return addresses. illegal is 1 when illegal_csr is 1, or is_mret is 1 and priv is not 3, or csrop is 101 and (priv is 0, or priv is 1 and tsr is 1), or csrop is 110 and (priv is 0, or priv is 1 and tvm is 1). trap is valid AND (xcpt OR illegal). c is cause when xcpt is 1, else 2. is_int is xcpt AND irq. t is 0 when is_int is 1, tval when xcpt is 1 and irq is 0, and inst when xcpt is 0. deleg is 1 when priv is not 3 and bit c of mideleg (when is_int is 1) or of medeleg (when is_int is 0) is 1. trap_s is trap AND deleg; trap_m is trap AND NOT deleg. mret (output) is valid AND NOT trap AND is_mret. sret is valid AND NOT trap AND csrop is 101. csr_we is valid AND NOT trap AND csrop is 010, 011 or 100. sfence is valid AND NOT trap AND csrop is 110. refetch is valid AND NOT trap AND csrop is 010, 011, 100, 110 or 111. redirect is trap OR mret OR sret OR refetch. kill is trap OR mret OR sret and nothing else: it is NOT redirect, so kill is 0 for a CSR refetch (a CSR instruction's own write-back must survive). Example: valid 1, xcpt 0, csrop 011 gives redirect 1 and kill 0. retire is valid AND NOT trap. The vector of a base register v is (v with bits 1:0 cleared) plus 4 times c when is_int is 1 and bit 0 of v is 1, else plus 0 (32 bits, wrapping). redirect_pc is the vector of mtvec when trap_m is 1; else the vector of stvec when trap_s is 1; else mepc when mret is 1; else sepc when sret is 1; else pc plus 4. epc is pc with bit 0 cleared. cause_val (32 bits) is c in bits 3:0 and is_int in bit 31, 0 elsewhere. tval_out is t. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: csr_mregs
blocks.description: The machine-mode CSRs other than mstatus and the counters. Held state, all 0 at reset: mtvec, mscratch, mepc, mcause, mtval (32 bits each), mie (12 bits), medeleg (16 bits), mideleg (12 bits), mcounteren (3 bits), mip_sw (12 bits, the software-writable bits of mip). The outputs show the held values. On each rising clock edge, the first that applies: rst is 1: everything becomes 0. trap_m is 1: mepc takes epc with bit 0 cleared, mcause takes cause_val and mtval takes tval. we is 1: by sel (6 bits), with v the 32-bit value nval: 3: medeleg takes v AND B3FF hexadecimal; 4: mideleg takes v AND 222; 5: mie takes v AND AAA; 6: mtvec takes v with bit 1 cleared; 7: mcounteren takes bits 2:0 of v; 8: mscratch takes v; 9: mepc takes v with bit 0 cleared; 10: mcause takes v; 11: mtval takes v; 12: mip_sw takes v AND 222; 28 (sie): mie takes (mie AND NOT mideleg) OR (v AND mideleg AND 222); 35 (sip): mip_sw takes (mip_sw AND NOT (mideleg AND 2)) OR (v AND mideleg AND 2); any other sel changes nothing. Otherwise nothing changes.

blocks.name: csr_sregs
blocks.description: The supervisor CSRs. Held state, all 0 at reset: stvec, sscratch, sepc, scause, stval, satp (32 bits each) and scounteren (3 bits). The outputs show the held values. On each rising clock edge, the first that applies: rst is 1: everything becomes 0. trap_s is 1: sepc takes epc with bit 0 cleared, scause takes cause_val and stval takes tval. we is 1: by sel (6 bits), with v the 32-bit value nval: 29: stvec takes v with bit 1 cleared; 30: scounteren takes bits 2:0 of v; 31: sscratch takes v; 32: sepc takes v with bit 0 cleared; 33: scause takes v; 34: stval takes v; 36: satp takes v AND 803FFFFF hexadecimal; any other sel changes nothing. Otherwise nothing changes.

blocks.name: counters
blocks.description: The cycle and retired-instruction counters, 64 bits each, both 0 at reset. Held state: mcycle and minstret (64 bits each). On each rising clock edge the first that applies: rst is 1: both become 0. we is 1 (a CSR write in write-back) and sel (6 bits) names a counter, with nval (32 bits) the value written: sel 13 writes the low word of mcycle, sel 15 its high word, sel 14 the low word of minstret, sel 16 its high word; the written word takes nval, the other word keeps its value, and the counter does not count on this edge (a write to minstret suppresses the increment of the instruction that writes it). Any other sel with we: nothing is written, and the counters count as below. Otherwise: mcycle goes up by one and minstret goes up by one when retire is 1 (both wrap at 64 bits). The outputs mcycle and minstret show the held values.

blocks.name: mip_merge
blocks.description: Combinational. The mip register as read (12 bits): bits 1, 5 and 9 are bits 1, 5 and 9 of mip_sw; bit 11 is meip, bit 7 is mtip, bit 3 is msip; every other bit is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: csr_rmux
blocks.description: Combinational. The value a CSR reads, by its number sel (6 bits). The CSR numbers (sel): 300 hexadecimal mstatus 1, 301 misa 2, 302 medeleg 3, 303 mideleg 4, 304 mie 5, 305 mtvec 6, 306 mcounteren 7, 340 mscratch 8, 341 mepc 9, 342 mcause 10, 343 mtval 11, 344 mip 12, B00 mcycle 13, B02 minstret 14, B80 mcycleh 15, B82 minstreth 16, C00 cycle 17, C01 time 18, C02 instret 19, C80 cycleh 20, C81 timeh 21, C82 instreth 22, F11 mvendorid 23, F12 marchid 24, F13 mimpid 25, F14 mhartid 26, 100 sstatus 27, 104 sie 28, 105 stvec 29, 106 scounteren 30, 140 sscratch 31, 141 sepc 32, 142 scause 33, 143 stval 34, 144 sip 35, 180 satp 36, 7A0 tselect 37, 7A1 tdata1 38, 7A2 tdata2 39, 7A3 tdata3 40, 320 mcountinhibit 41 (these five are hard-wired: they read 0 and ignore writes), 3A0 pmpcfg0 42, 3B0 pmpaddr0 43; every other address is 0 (no register). rdata (32 bits): 1 mstatus; 2 the constant 40141105 hexadecimal (misa); 3 medeleg; 4 mideleg; 5 mie; 6 mtvec; 7 mcounteren; 8 mscratch; 9 mepc; 10 mcause; 11 mtval; 12 mip; 13 bits 31:0 of mcycle; 14 bits 31:0 of minstret; 15 bits 63:32 of mcycle; 16 bits 63:32 of minstret; 17 bits 31:0 of mcycle; 18 bits 31:0 of mtime; 19 bits 31:0 of minstret; 20 bits 63:32 of mcycle; 21 bits 63:32 of mtime; 22 bits 63:32 of minstret; 23, 24 and 25 the constant 0; 26 hartid; 27 mstatus AND 000C0122 hexadecimal (sstatus); 28 mie AND mideleg (sie); 29 stvec; 30 scounteren; 31 sscratch; 32 sepc; 33 scause; 34 stval; 35 mip AND mideleg (sip); 36 satp; 42 pmpcfg0; 43 pmpaddr0 (both from the PMP registers, the inputs pmpcfg0 and pmpaddr0 of 32 bits); any other sel 0. Inputs narrower than 32 bits are zero-extended. Widths: mcycle, minstret and mtime 64 bits; medeleg 16; mideleg, mie and mip 12; mcounteren and scounteren 3; hartid 2; the others 32. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: status_we
blocks.description: Combinational. The write strobes of mstatus and sstatus. we_m is 1 when csr_we is 1 and sel (6 bits) is 1; we_s is 1 when csr_we is 1 and sel is 27; both are 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: satp_split
blocks.description: Combinational. The fields of satp (32 bits): mode is bit 31; ppn (22 bits) is bits 21:0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: xlate_on
blocks.description: Combinational. Whether addresses are translated. priv (2 bits: 0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine); mprv and mpp (2 bits) from mstatus; satp_mode is bit 31 of satp. dpriv (2 bits), the privilege of data accesses, is mpp when mprv is 1 and priv is 3, and priv otherwise. xlate_i is 1 when satp_mode is 1 and priv is not 3. xlate_d is 1 when satp_mode is 1 and dpriv is not 3. kind_i (2 bits) is always 00 (the access kind of an instruction fetch). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: dkind
blocks.description: Combinational, in the execute stage. valid is 1 for a real instruction; memsrc 01 means a load; memwrite 1 a store; is_amo 1 an atomic instruction, amo_op (4 bits) its code (0001 is load-reserved). access is 1 when valid is 1 and (memsrc is 01 or memwrite is 1 or is_amo is 1). store is 1 when memwrite is 1, or is_amo is 1 and amo_op is not 0001. kind (2 bits) is 10 when store is 1 and 01 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: dfault_gate
blocks.description: Combinational, in the execute stage. The data translation looks up the result address of every instruction, but only an instruction that reads or writes memory can fault on it, and only while data accesses are translated. access is 1 when the instruction does (dkind's access). xlate is 1 when data accesses are translated. pf and af are the translation's page fault and access fault for the instruction's result address. pf_o is 1 when pf is 1 and access is 1 and xlate is 1, and 0 otherwise; af_o is 1 when af is 1 and access is 1 and xlate is 1, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ifault
blocks.description: Combinational, after the fetch aligner. A fetch that faulted enters the pipeline as a reserved instruction word. inst (32 bits) and is16 are the aligner's output; pc is the fetch address; word_lo the word read at pc; xlate is 1 when fetches are translated; lo_pf and lo_af say the word at pc gave a page fault or an access fault, hi_pf and hi_af the same for the next word. need_hi is 1 when bit 1 of pc is 1 and bits 17:16 of word_lo are 11. When xlate is 1 and (lo_pf or lo_af is 1): inst_out is 0000000B hexadecimal with bits 14:12 set to 001 when lo_pf is 1, else 010 (that is 0000100B or 0000200B), and is16_out is 0. Else when xlate is 1 and need_hi is 1 and (hi_pf or hi_af is 1): inst_out is the reserved word with bits 14:12 001 when hi_pf is 1, else 010, and bit 20 also 1 (0010100B or 0010200B; nothing of word_lo or inst is copied into it), and is16_out is 0. Otherwise inst_out is inst and is16_out is is16. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: mmu_ctl
blocks.description: Combinational. Whether the core must wait for a page-table walk, and what to walk. need_hi is 1 when bit 1 of pc is 1 and bits 17:16 of word_lo (the word fetched at pc) are 11: the instruction continues into the next word. lm is xlate_i AND lo_miss. hm is xlate_i AND NOT lo_miss AND need_hi AND hi_miss. dm is xlate_d AND d_access AND d_miss. stall is ptw_busy OR lm OR hm OR dm. walk_start is NOT ptw_busy AND (lm OR hm OR dm). walk_va (32 bits) is d_va when dm is 1; else pc when lm is 1; else hi_addr when hm is 1; else 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: pa_mux_ilo
blocks.description: Combinational. The physical address. When xlate is 1, pa is ppa (20 bits) in bits 31:12 and bits 11:0 of va in bits 11:0; when xlate is 0, pa is va. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: pa_mux_ihi
blocks.description: Combinational. The physical address. When xlate is 1, pa is ppa (20 bits) in bits 31:12 and bits 11:0 of va in bits 11:0; when xlate is 0, pa is va. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: pa_mux_d
blocks.description: Combinational. The physical address. When xlate is 1, pa is ppa (20 bits) in bits 31:12 and bits 11:0 of va in bits 11:0; when xlate is 0, pa is va. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: perm_check_ilo
blocks.description: Combinational. Whether an access is refused by a leaf page-table entry. kind (2 bits): 00 instruction fetch, 01 load, 10 or 11 store. priv (2 bits): 0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine. sum and mxr are the mstatus bits. flags are the low 8 bits of a page-table entry: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, U bit 4, G bit 5, A bit 6, D bit 7. fault is 1 when any of these holds, else 0. A machine-mode access (priv 3) never faults here: machine mode does not translate, so fault is 0 whatever the flags. Otherwise fault is 1 when any of these holds: priv is 0 and U is 0; priv is 1 and U is 1 and (kind is a fetch or sum is 0); the access is not allowed (a fetch needs X; a load needs R, or X when mxr is 1; a store needs W); A is 0; the access is a store and D is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: perm_check_ihi
blocks.description: Combinational. Whether an access is refused by a leaf page-table entry. kind (2 bits): 00 instruction fetch, 01 load, 10 or 11 store. priv (2 bits): 0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine. sum and mxr are the mstatus bits. flags are the low 8 bits of a page-table entry: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, U bit 4, G bit 5, A bit 6, D bit 7. fault is 1 when any of these holds, else 0. A machine-mode access (priv 3) never faults here: machine mode does not translate, so fault is 0 whatever the flags. Otherwise fault is 1 when any of these holds: priv is 0 and U is 0; priv is 1 and U is 1 and (kind is a fetch or sum is 0); the access is not allowed (a fetch needs X; a load needs R, or X when mxr is 1; a store needs W); A is 0; the access is a store and D is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: perm_check_d
blocks.description: Combinational. Whether an access is refused by a leaf page-table entry. kind (2 bits): 00 instruction fetch, 01 load, 10 or 11 store. priv (2 bits): 0 user, 1 supervisor, 3 machine. sum and mxr are the mstatus bits. flags are the low 8 bits of a page-table entry: V bit 0, R bit 1, W bit 2, X bit 3, U bit 4, G bit 5, A bit 6, D bit 7. fault is 1 when any of these holds, else 0. A machine-mode access (priv 3) never faults here: machine mode does not translate, so fault is 0 whatever the flags. Otherwise fault is 1 when any of these holds: priv is 0 and U is 0; priv is 1 and U is 1 and (kind is a fetch or sum is 0); the access is not allowed (a fetch needs X; a load needs R, or X when mxr is 1; a store needs W); A is 0; the access is a store and D is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: xfault_ilo
blocks.description: Combinational. The result of one address translation. hit, and perm_fault (the access is refused by the entry that hit); wfault, waccess and wvpn (20 bits) are the walker's held fault, whether it was an access fault, and the page it was for; va (32 bits) is this lookup's address. held is wfault AND (wvpn equals bits 31:12 of va). pf is perm_fault when hit is 1, and held AND NOT waccess when hit is 0. af is NOT hit AND held AND waccess. miss is NOT hit AND NOT held. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: xfault_ihi
blocks.description: Combinational. The result of one address translation. hit, and perm_fault (the access is refused by the entry that hit); wfault, waccess and wvpn (20 bits) are the walker's held fault, whether it was an access fault, and the page it was for; va (32 bits) is this lookup's address. held is wfault AND (wvpn equals bits 31:12 of va). pf is perm_fault when hit is 1, and held AND NOT waccess when hit is 0. af is NOT hit AND held AND waccess. miss is NOT hit AND NOT held. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: xfault_d
blocks.description: Combinational. The result of one address translation. hit, and perm_fault (the access is refused by the entry that hit); wfault, waccess and wvpn (20 bits) are the walker's held fault, whether it was an access fault, and the page it was for; va (32 bits) is this lookup's address. held is wfault AND (wvpn equals bits 31:12 of va). pf is perm_fault when hit is 1, and held AND NOT waccess when hit is 0. af is NOT hit AND held AND waccess. miss is NOT hit AND NOT held. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: need_hi_gen
blocks.description: Combinational. need_hi is 1 when bit 1 of pc (32 bits) is 1 and bits 17:16 of word_lo (32 bits, the word fetched at pc) are 11 (binary): the instruction at pc is 32 bits wide and continues into the next word. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fencei_gate
blocks.description: Combinational. fence_i is 1 when valid is 1 and csrop (3 bits) is 111 (binary) and trap_m is 0 and trap_s is 0: a fence.i instruction that retires. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_resmux
blocks.description: Combinational. The execute stage's result: y (32 bits) is from_fp when sel is 1 and from_alu when sel is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_fp
blocks.description: Combinational. inst (32 bits) is the instruction text from the fetch aligner (a compressed instruction is in its low 16 bits) and word_in (32 bits) is the 32-bit instruction the integer expander made of it. word_out is word_in, except for eight compressed floating-point loads and stores, for which it is the equivalent 32-bit instruction. They are recognised by bits 1:0 and bits 15:13 of inst: bits 1:0 = 00 with bits 15:13 = 001 (C.FLD), 011 (C.FLW), 101 (C.FSD) or 111 (C.FSW); bits 1:0 = 10 with bits 15:13 = 001 (C.FLDSP), 011 (C.FLWSP), 101 (C.FSDSP) or 111 (C.FSWSP). Every other value of bits 1:0 and 15:13 (so also every 32-bit instruction, whose bits 1:0 are 11) gives word_in. Let rp1 be 8 plus bits 9:7 of inst and rp2 be 8 plus bits 4:2 of inst (5-bit register numbers), rd be bits 11:7 of inst and rs2 be bits 6:2 of inst. For the loads (word_out has opcode 0000111): C.FLD and C.FLW: bits 31:20 of word_out are the zero-extended offset uimm, bits 19:15 are rp1, bits 11:7 are rp2; C.FLDSP and C.FLWSP: bits 31:20 are the zero-extended offset uimm, bits 19:15 are 2 (the stack pointer, 00010), bits 11:7 are rd. Bits 14:12 of word_out (the funct3) are 011 for C.FLD and C.FLDSP and 010 for C.FLW and C.FLWSP. For the stores (word_out has opcode 0100111): bits 14:12 are 011 for C.FSD and C.FSDSP and 010 for C.FSW and C.FSWSP; bits 31:25 are uimm[11:5] and bits 11:7 are uimm[4:0] (the offset split as in an S-type instruction); bits 19:15 are rp1 and bits 24:20 are rp2 for C.FSD and C.FSW; bits 19:15 are 2 (00010) and bits 24:20 are rs2 for C.FSDSP and C.FSWSP. The offset uimm: C.FLD and C.FSD: uimm[7:6] is inst[6:5], uimm[5:3] is inst[12:10], every other bit 0. C.FLW and C.FSW: uimm[6] is inst[5], uimm[5:3] is inst[12:10], uimm[2] is inst[6], every other bit 0. C.FLDSP: uimm[5] is inst[12], uimm[4:3] is inst[6:5], uimm[8:6] is inst[4:2], every other bit 0. C.FLWSP: uimm[5] is inst[12], uimm[4:2] is inst[6:4], uimm[7:6] is inst[3:2], every other bit 0. C.FSDSP: uimm[5:3] is inst[12:10], uimm[8:6] is inst[9:7], every other bit 0. C.FSWSP: uimm[5:2] is inst[12:9], uimm[7:6] is inst[8:7], every other bit 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_dec
blocks.description: Combinational, in the decode stage. inst (32 bits) is the instruction word, fs (2 bits) the floating-point unit state (0 means off) and frm (3 bits) the dynamic rounding mode. Fields of inst: opcode is bits 6:0, f3 is bits 14:12, fmt is bits 26:25, f5 is bits 31:27, rs2f is bits 24:20. rm_ok is 1 when f3 is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4, or when f3 is 7 and frm is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 (f3 equal to 5 or 6 and the rest are not ok). The word is a FLOATING-POINT INSTRUCTION when it is one of these: (load) opcode 0000111 with f3 010 or 011; (store) opcode 0100111 with f3 010 or 011; (fused) opcode 1000011, 1000111, 1001011 or 1001111, with fmt 00 or 01 and rm_ok; (arithmetic) opcode 1010011 with fmt 00 or 01 and, by f5: 00000, 00001, 00010 or 00011 with rm_ok; 01011 with rs2f 00000 and rm_ok; 00100 with f3 000, 001 or 010; 00101 with f3 000 or 001; 01000 with rm_ok and either (fmt 00 and rs2f 00001) or (fmt 01 and rs2f 00000); 10100 with f3 000, 001 or 010; 11000 with rs2f 00000 or 00001 and rm_ok; 11010 with rs2f 00000 or 00001 and rm_ok; 11100 with rs2f 00000 and (f3 001, or f3 000 and fmt 00); 11110 with rs2f 00000, f3 000 and fmt 00. is_fp is 1 when the word is a floating-point instruction and fs is not 0. is_dw is 1 when is_fp is 1 and opcode is 0000111 or 0100111 and f3 is 011 (a double-precision load or store). dec_inst (32 bits) is inst when is_fp is 0, and otherwise an integer instruction with the same register fields, built so that the integer decoder treats it as a harmless instruction: for a load, the word with bits 31:15 of inst, funct3 010, rd 00000 and opcode 0000011; for a store, the word with bits 31:7 of inst, funct3 010 in bits 14:12 and opcode 0100011 (bits 31:15 and 11:7 are those of inst); for a fused instruction and for an arithmetic instruction whose f5 is not 10100, 11000 or 11100: bits 31:25 are 0000000, bits 24:20 are those of inst, bits 19:15 are those of inst, funct3 000, rd 00000 and opcode 0110011; for an arithmetic instruction whose f5 is 10100, 11000 or 11100: the same, but with rd being bits 11:7 of inst. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_dwseq
blocks.description: Splits a double-precision load or store into two word accesses, in the decode stage. is_dw is 1 when the instruction in decode is a double-precision load or store, valid is 1 when it is a real instruction, xcpt is 1 when it already carries an exception; stall is 1 when the execute stage holds (decode cannot hand its instruction over) and flush is 1 when the execute stage takes a bubble this cycle. dw is is_dw AND valid AND NOT xcpt. Held state, 0 at reset: half2 (1 bit). Outputs, from the state and inputs, before the edge: half2 as held; hold is dw AND NOT half2 (the instruction stays in decode for a second pass); dwsel (2 bits) is 00 when dw is 0, 01 when dw is 1 and half2 is 0, and 10 when dw is 1 and half2 is 1; imm_out (32 bits) is imm_in plus 4 (wrapping) when dw is 1 and half2 is 1, and imm_in otherwise. accept is NOT stall AND NOT flush. On each rising clock edge, after reset (reset sets half2 to 0): when flush is 1, half2 becomes 0; otherwise when dw is 1 and accept is 1, half2 becomes NOT half2; otherwise when dw is 0, half2 becomes 0; otherwise half2 keeps its value.

blocks.name: fp_hazard
blocks.description: Combinational. Makes a floating-point instruction in decode wait while an older floating-point instruction that writes a floating-point register is in the execute or memory stage, and merges the extra hold of a double-word access into the hazard unit's outputs. stall and flush_id_ex are the hazard unit's outputs, md_stall is 1 while the execute stage holds its instruction, dw_hold is 1 while a double-word instruction stays in decode for its second pass, id_valid is 1 when decode holds a real instruction, id_is_fp is 1 when that instruction is a floating-point one, half2 is 1 in the second pass of a double-word instruction. A word is a WRITER when its opcode (bits 6:0) is 0000111, 1000011, 1000111, 1001011, 1001111 or 1010011. ex_wr is ex_valid AND ex_inst (32 bits) is a writer; mem_wr is mem_valid AND mem_inst (32 bits) is a writer. wait is id_valid AND id_is_fp AND NOT half2 AND (ex_wr OR mem_wr). stall_out is stall OR dw_hold OR wait. flush_out is flush_id_ex OR (wait AND NOT md_stall). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_pipe
blocks.description: The floating-point side of the pipeline registers: it carries, with an instruction, its half-select dwsel (2 bits) from decode to execute, and the floating-point result of execute (fres 64 bits, flags 5 bits, wrf 1 bit) on through the memory stage to write-back, along with dwsel. Three register stages, all 0 after reset. Decode to execute (dwsel_ex): on each rising clock edge, when rst is 1 or flush_ex is 1 it becomes 0; otherwise when stall_ex is 1 it keeps its value; otherwise it becomes dwsel_id. Execute to memory (dwsel_m, fres_m, flags_m, wrf_m): when rst is 1 or flush_mem is 1 they become 0; otherwise they become dwsel_ex, fres_ex, flags_ex and wrf_ex. Memory to write-back (dwsel_wb, fres_wb, flags_wb, wrf_wb): when rst is 1 or flush_wb is 1 they become 0; otherwise they become dwsel_m, fres_m, flags_m and wrf_m (the values held before the edge). Every output is the held value of the register of that name, with no combinational path from an input to an output.

blocks.name: fp_exdec
blocks.description: Combinational, in the execute stage. inst (32 bits) is the instruction word, valid is 1 for a real instruction, xcpt is 1 when it carries an exception, frm (3 bits) is the dynamic rounding mode. Fields: opcode is bits 6:0, f3 bits 14:12, fmt bits 26:25, f5 bits 31:27, rs2f bits 24:20. active is valid AND NOT xcpt. is_fpu is active AND opcode is 1000011, 1000111, 1001011, 1001111 or 1010011. is_fst is active AND opcode is 0100111 (a floating-point store). int_dest is is_fpu AND opcode is 1010011 AND f5 is 10100, 11000 or 11100 (the result goes to an integer register). ra1 is bits 19:15 of inst, ra2 is bits 24:20 and ra3 is bits 31:27 (always). op (5 bits): for opcode 1000011 it is 5, for 1000111 it is 6, for 1001011 it is 7, for 1001111 it is 8; for opcode 1010011, by f5: 00000 gives 0, 00001 gives 1, 00010 gives 2, 00011 gives 3, 01011 gives 4, 00100 gives 9 plus f3, 00101 gives 12 plus f3, 01000 gives 22 when fmt is 00 and 23 otherwise, 10100 gives 14 when f3 is 010, 15 when f3 is 001 and 16 otherwise, 11000 gives 18 plus bit 0 of rs2f, 11010 gives 20 plus bit 0 of rs2f, 11100 gives 17 when f3 is 001 and 24 otherwise, 11110 gives 25; every other word gives 0. dbl is bit 0 of fmt (bit 25 of inst), except that it is 0 when opcode is 1010011 and f5 is 01000. rm (3 bits): when the word is a fused instruction (opcode 1000011, 1000111, 1001011 or 1001111) or has opcode 1010011 with f5 equal to 00000, 00001, 00010, 00011, 01011, 01000, 11000 or 11010, rm is frm when f3 is 111 and f3 otherwise; for every other word rm is 000. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_seq
blocks.description: Sequencer between the execute stage and the floating-point unit. is_fpu is 1 while the instruction in the execute stage needs the unit. The unit pulses done (for one cycle) when it has a result, with fres_in (64 bits), ires_in (32 bits), flags_in (5 bits) and wrf_in (1 bit) valid in that cycle. Held state, all 0 at reset: st (2 bits: 0 idle, 1 running, 2 finished) and the latched result fres (64 bits), ires (32 bits), flags (5 bits) and wrf (1 bit). Outputs, from the state and inputs, before the edge: start is is_fpu AND st is 0; busy is is_fpu AND st is not 2; fres, ires, flags and wrf are the latched values. On each rising clock edge, after reset (rst sets everything to 0): when st is 0 and is_fpu is 1, st becomes 1; when st is 1 and done is 1, the latched values become fres_in, ires_in, flags_in and wrf_in and st becomes 2; when st is 2, st becomes 0; otherwise nothing changes. (A finished result stays latched until the next result is latched.)

blocks.name: fp_xcpt
blocks.description: Combinational, in the execute stage: the alignment trap of a double-precision access, merged into the execute stage's exception. xcpt_in, cause_in (4 bits), tval_in (32 bits) and memwrite_in are the exception unit's outputs, is_store is 1 when the instruction is a store, dwsel (2 bits) is 01 in the first pass of a double-word access, 10 in the second and 00 otherwise, addr (32 bits) is the access's address. bad is NOT xcpt_in AND dwsel is 01 AND bits 2:0 of addr are not 000. xcpt is xcpt_in OR bad. cause is, when bad is 1, 6 when is_store is 1 and 4 otherwise, and cause_in when bad is 0. tval is addr when bad is 1 and tval_in otherwise. memwrite_out is memwrite_in AND NOT bad. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fregfile
blocks.description: Floating-point register file: 32 registers of 64 bits (register 0 is an ordinary register). Held state: the 32 registers, which are not cleared by reset (their contents before the first write are not defined). Three read ports: rdata1, rdata2 and rdata3 (64 bits each) are the contents, before the clock edge, of the registers numbered ra1, ra2 and ra3 (5 bits each); a read does not see a write that happens at the coming edge. Two write enables with one address: on each rising clock edge, when we_lo is 1 bits 31:0 of the register numbered waddr become wdata_lo (32 bits), and when we_hi is 1 bits 63:32 of that register become wdata_hi (32 bits); the two halves are independent.

blocks.name: fp_stmux
blocks.description: Combinational. The data of a store: y (32 bits) is from_core when is_fst is 0. When is_fst is 1, y is bits 63:32 of fdata (64 bits) when dwsel (2 bits) is 10 and bits 31:0 of fdata otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_wb
blocks.description: Combinational, in the write-back stage: what the instruction there writes into the floating-point register file and the status. inst (32 bits) is the instruction, commit is 1 when it retires (it is real and raises no exception), dwsel (2 bits) is 00, 01 or 10 (whole register, first word of a double-word access, second word), mem_rdata (32 bits) is the value its load read, fres (64 bits), flags (5 bits) and wrf (1 bit) are the result of the floating-point unit. opcode is bits 6:0 of inst. is_load is commit AND opcode is 0000111. is_op is commit AND opcode is 1000011, 1000111, 1001011, 1001111 or 1010011. waddr is bits 11:7 of inst. we_lo is 1 when is_load is 1 and dwsel is not 10, or when is_op is 1 and wrf is 1. we_hi is 1 when is_load is 1 and dwsel is not 01, or when is_op is 1 and wrf is 1. wdata_lo is mem_rdata for a load and bits 31:0 of fres otherwise. wdata_hi is, for a load, mem_rdata when dwsel is 10 and FFFFFFFF (hexadecimal) otherwise, and bits 63:32 of fres when it is not a load. flags_set (5 bits) is flags when is_op is 1 and 0 otherwise. dirty_set is 1 when is_load is 1, or when is_op is 1 and (wrf is 1 or flags is not 0). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fp_csr
blocks.description: The floating-point control and status registers and the FS field of mstatus, with the read and legality patches for them. Held state, 0 at reset: fflags (5 bits), frm (3 bits) and fs (2 bits; 0 off, 1 initial, 2 clean, 3 dirty). inst (32 bits) is the instruction in write-back; addr is bits 31:20 of inst (the CSR address); csrop (3 bits) is its CSR operation: it accesses a CSR when csrop is 001 (read only), 010, 011 or 100 (binary). csr_we is 1 when a CSR write takes effect now; nval (32 bits) is the value written. flags_set (5 bits) and dirty_set come from a retiring floating-point instruction. Outputs from the state and inputs, before the edge: fs, frm as held. rdata_in (32 bits) is the CSR read value of the rest of the core and illegal_in the rest of the core's illegal-CSR flag. rdata_out is: for addr 001 (hexadecimal) the 5-bit fflags zero-extended; for addr 002 frm zero-extended; for addr 003 frm in bits 7:5 and fflags in bits 4:0, zero elsewhere; for addr 300 or 100 rdata_in with bits 14:13 set to fs and bit 31 set to 1 when fs is 3 (the other bits of rdata_in kept); for addr 301 rdata_in with bits 3 and 5 set to 1; for every other addr rdata_in. illegal_out is, when csrop accesses a CSR and addr is 001, 002 or 003, 1 when fs is 0 and 0 otherwise; in every other case it is illegal_in. On each rising clock edge, after reset: when csr_we is 1: for addr 001 fflags becomes bits 4:0 of nval and fs becomes 3; for addr 002 frm becomes bits 2:0 of nval and fs becomes 3; for addr 003 frm becomes bits 7:5 of nval, fflags becomes bits 4:0 of nval and fs becomes 3; for addr 300 or 100 fs becomes bits 14:13 of nval; for every other addr nothing changes. When csr_we is 0: fflags becomes fflags OR flags_set, and when dirty_set is 1 fs becomes 3.

blocks.name: fp_or2
blocks.description: Combinational. y is a OR b. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: fpu
blocks.description: RV32 F and D floating-point unit (curated barg_fpu)
